name: Trinidad and Tobago
headline: Trinidad and Tobago: −0.5% growth in 2025, 1.0% inflation, debt 84% of GDP
sections: Trinidad and Tobago is a $25.9 billion economy (2025), the world's 124th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −0.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $37K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 14.4% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 1.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.5% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 8.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 84% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −5.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +5.0% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Net FDI inflows were −3.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 81% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 73.6 years (2024). Population: 1.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
